title: Browser module loading and CORS requirements
learningObjectives: Explain browser module loading and cors requirements and build modular, event-driven browser code.

understand.concept: Browser ES modules are loaded with script type=module and use strict module semantics. Module scripts are deferred by default. Browsers apply CORS rules to module fetches, and modules should be served over HTTP(S) rather than opened as file URLs. Correct MIME types and allowed origins matter.
understand.whyItMatters: A module import can fail even when the file exists if the server, MIME type, or CORS configuration is wrong. Local development should use a development server.
understand.analogy: A module is a package delivered through a controlled loading route; the browser checks whether the route and response are suitable.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; module loading and DOM event behaviour follow web platform standards.

explain.narrative: The browser loads app.js as a module and resolves its relative import. Files should be served from a web server with correct headers.

examples.code:
<!-- index.html -->
<script type='module' src='./app.js'></script>
<!-- app.js -->
import {start} from './start.js';
start();
examples.explanation: The browser loads app.js as a module and resolves its relative import. Files should be served from a web server with correct headers.
examples.expectedOutput: Browser console output demonstrates module or event behaviour; DOM examples require matching elements.

practise.guidedTask: Run a two-module page using a local development server. Inspect the Network panel for status, MIME type, and CORS errors.
practise.independentTask: Build a small feature using explicit module boundaries or DOM event handling. Test keyboard, pointer, dynamic content, and failure cases as appropriate.
hints: Keep module responsibilities and public exports clear.
Preserve native keyboard and form behaviour.

questions.prompt: How should browser ES modules normally be loaded?
options: Using script type=module from an HTTP(S) server
questions.answer: Using script type=module from an HTTP(S) server
questions.explanation: Module scripts use type=module and should be served with appropriate HTTP(S) responses.

questions.prompt: What is a good principle for modular event-driven code?
options: Use clear contracts and preserve expected browser behaviour
Stop all propagation for every event
Expose every internal module binding globally
questions.answer: Use clear contracts and preserve expected browser behaviour
questions.explanation: Explicit interfaces and predictable event handling reduce coupling and preserve usability.
